To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the backward Drell-Yan cross section is sensitive to nuclear effects, especially the intrinsic transverse momenta, and that this observable cannot discriminate between the different formalisms, i.e., k{sub T}-factorization and the color dipole model.

the backward Drell-Yan process in proton-nuclei collisions at RHIC and LHC energies is sensitive to the intrinsic transverse momenta of quarks and gluons, and that the ratio between the Drell-Yan cross sections in p(d)-A collisions to those in p-p collisions is not sensitive to the particular shape of color dipole cross sections.

the backward dilepton production is sensitive to intrinsic transverse momentum, and the ratio between proton-lead collisions and proton-proton collisions is independent of the shape of the color-dipole cross section.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of Drell–Yan pairs at backward rapidities in proton–nucleus collisions at RHIC and the LHC.
the study of the backward Drell-Yan production in proton-nuclei collisions at RHIC and LHC energies.
the study of the production of a pair of back-to-back jets in e+e- annihilation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the k{sub t} factorization is the appropriate formalism to describe the Drell-Yan process at backward rapidities.
the kT factorization and the color dipole approaches are complementary and that both are able to describe backward Drell-Yan data at RHIC and LHC energies.
, in the case of backward Drell-Yan production, the k{sub t} factorization approach is more suitable for describing the experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
backward Drell-Yan production at backward rapidity in proton-nuclei collisions is sensitive to the intrinsic k{sup T}.
the backward dilepton production is sensitive to nuclear effects, and that the color dipole and kT factorization models can be discriminated.
the backward Drell-Yan process is a good probe of the small x behavior of the gluon and the quark distribution function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ratio between proton-nucleus and proton-proton collisions for the Drell-Yan process at backward rapidities, in the kinematical range accessible at Relativistic Ion Collider and Lattice Hadron Collider, can be used to test the k{sub t} factorization approach and to study the nuclear effects on the target gluon distribution.

the backward dilepton production in p(d)-A collisions is sensitive to the nuclear parton distribution function and the intrinsic transverse k{sub T}, but it is not affected by the color glass condensatetheory.

the k{sub t} factorization and the color dipole formalisms give similar results for the ratio of backward Drell-Yan processes in p(d)-A/p-p collisions, but the k{subt} approach is sensitive to the intrinsic k{t} and to the nuclear shadowing effects.
